grammar.label: present perfect continuous — form and use
grammar.meaning: an activity that began in the past and is still going on, or has just stopped with a visible result

explanation.en: Use have/has been + -ing for an activity that started earlier and continues now. The focus is on the activity and its duration, not on a finished result.
explanation.uz: Ilgari boshlanib hozir ham davom etayotgan ish uchun have/has been + -ing ishlatiladi. E'tibor natijaga emas, jarayonga va uning davomiyligiga qaratiladi.

grammar.positive_example: I have been waiting for an hour.
grammar.negative_example: I am waiting for an hour.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek tilida hozirgi zamon ishlatiladi ('bir soatdan beri kutyapman'), shuning uchun o'quvchi 'I am waiting for an hour' deb xato qiladi.
l1_notes.ru: В русском тоже настоящее время ('жду час'), отсюда та же ошибка.

grammar.label: present perfect simple vs continuous
grammar.form: have done vs have been doing
grammar.meaning: a completed result against an ongoing or recent activity

explanation.en: The simple form counts results: 'I have read three chapters.' The continuous form measures activity: 'I have been reading all afternoon.'
explanation.uz: Oddiy shakl natijani sanaydi: 'I have read three chapters.' Davomli shakl jarayonni o'lchaydi: 'I have been reading all afternoon.'

grammar.positive_example: I have been painting, so my hands are dirty.
grammar.negative_example: I have painted, so my hands are dirty.

l1_notes.uz: Ikkala shakl ham o'zbekchada bitta shaklga to'g'ri kelishi mumkin; farqni ma'no belgilaydi.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: How long have you been learning Uzbek now?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Four years. I have been taking lessons since I arrived.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: The accuracy has. The fluency is still slow.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: You have learned a lot. I have heard you in the market.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: I have learned about two thousand new items. That is easy.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Patience. I have been working on the same mistakes for months.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: My teacher says that too. Progress is gradual, never fast.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: My tutor says the same. She has been teaching for twenty years.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Then she knows. Daily practice beats a long lesson once a week.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: I have been trying that since March, and she is right.
